newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at intraday high vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at an intraday high and an 11-week high close of 8.2929 against the U.S. dollar on Monday in Shanghai, up from 8.2933 last Friday, due to expectations it will rise further still, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2931.
The yuan opened unchanged at an intraday low of 8.2933 and moved in a narrow range around 8.2930 for most of the session.
Trading was active early in the session but slow in late trading, with most business done at 8.2931, traders said.
Dealers said the market widely expected the yuan to rise further as a result of its strong uptrend since Monday of last week.
One dealer said the belief resulted in active buying of the local currency active, particularly early in the session.
The lack of central bank intervention to depress the yuan was also helping its rise, he said.
A second dealer said the yuan had now moved back to the 8.2900-8.2930 level it hit in mid-February. "It needs a technical correction before it can go any further," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2930 on Tuesday.
The yuan fell to 6.9854 from 6.7580 against 100 Japanese yen and edged down at 1.0717 from 1.0715 vs the Hong Kong dollar.
